messages:
nina: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC: we keep seeing bench variance between intake mini-bench runs. proposing a small change to the pipeline to categorize variance and act accordingly. thoughts?

sam: Can you sketch the categories? is this noise vs deterministic regression vs tokenizer-induced?

nina: Yep. My thinking: three buckets -> noise (statistical), regressions (quality diffs), and contract mismatches (tokenizer/seqlen). We treat them differently.

leo: For noise, we could retry the mini-bench N=3 times and use median p95. For regressions, require a rerun with the full bench and attach diffs.

bench-bot: bench-bot: recent mini-bench for model:dialogue-lite-v0 -> p95=280ms, p95(retry2)=298ms, p95(retry3)=285ms, coeff_var=0.04.

tara: Coeff var 0.04 sounds fine. We should define thresholds: coeff_var > 0.08 => mark UNSTABLE and trigger full bench.

nina: Agreed. Also want a small change to golden set: expand it with 10 medium-tail inputs (longer seqlen, nested JSON prompts) because many false passes are short-seq only.

sam: How do we add them without exploding bench cost? Maybe only include extra golden samples in mini-bench when effective seqlen distribution in model manifest indicates heavy tail.

leo: Could derive seqlen profile from the tokenizer step in intake. Add histogram buckets: [0-32,33-128,129-512,>512]. If >10% in >128 then include tail golden samples.

nina: Good. Also propose we compute a tiny quality delta metric: edit-distance on normalized outputs + embed-sim fallback. If quality delta > threshold on golden inputs, mark FAIL_QUALITY.

bench-bot: bench-bot: golden-check for dialogue-lite-v0 -> lev_norm=0.03, embed_sim=0.92 -> PASS.

sam: We need to be careful: some transforms (formatting tokens, whitespace) can spike edit-distance. Normalize by tokenization and whitespace and strip deterministic markers.

leo: Operational: rollout notify-only for 2 weeks. Add flags on model-card: perf:unstable-variance, perf:tail-risk. Solutions can triage.

nina: One more: adapters/LoRA again. If model manifest contains adapters: run warm-up deserialization step and measure deserialization_time_ms; if >50ms add adapter_penalty to p95 before comparing to route_budget.

tara: That will catch the big source of unexpected latency. Also log adapter sizes so SRE can correlate.

sam: Do we store all retries and diffs in the intake artifact? yes/no?

nina: Yes. Intake artifact should include raw timings, tokenization hist, golden diffs, and the three-run p95 set. Small JSON blob attached to model entry.

bench-bot: bench-bot: action plan created in intake ticket #INT-4821. notify-mode enabled for model-group: experimental.

leo: +1. I'll draft the tiny RFC text and add thresholds. Nina, can you own golden sample selection? Tara can be owner for normalization rules?

nina: Yep. I'll put a PR for golden-set additions and a script to sample candidate tail cases from production traces (anonymized).

tara: I'll write normalization heuristics and a short unit test harness for the edit-distance sanitizer.

sam: Sounds good. Let's include snippets in the RFC with examples and the exact thresholds: coeff_var>0.08, retry_count=3, adapter_deser_ms>50, tail_bucket_threshold=0.1.

nina: Perfect. I'll open the RFC draft and ping the channel.
